newsitem.title: GERMANY: Balladur urges Germany and France to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Balladur urges Germany and France to cut rates.

text.p: France and Germany should cut interest rates to counter the overvaluation of their currencies against the dollar, former French premier Edouard Balladur said in a newspaper interview.
"The dollar is at least 10 percent undervalued," Balladur told the Handelsblatt and the Wall Street Journal. Excerpts of the interview were made available in advance by Handelsblatt.
Weak growth, high unemployment and serious budget deficits could undermine the future single European currency if the overvaluation of the mark and franc is not corrected, he said.
"Under current conditions, interest rate cuts would not mean additional inflation dangers," he said. "The problem now is not inflation but stagnation. But how can one explain that to the Germans?"
Governments should prescribe exchange-rate targets for central banks, and the central banks' monetary policies should heed those targets, he said.
"If that is not possible, too much power will be concentrated in the central banks," he said.
The mark-franc exchange, however, is perfect, he said. A devaluation of the franc against the mark could disrupt convergence and hamper the introduction of the single currency.
